newsitem.title: UK: Ex-Merrill metals trader Becker issues statement.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Merrill metals trader Becker issues statement.

text.p: Independent metals trader Wolfgang Becker said he has suffered from what he called inaccurate press comment after his former employer, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, settled a dispute with Chilean state copper firm Codelco.
Merrill Lynch last month agreed to pay Codelco $25 million after the Chilean firm lost $170 million in 1994 in copper trades carried out by its former top trader Juan Pablo Davila.

Merrill Lynch, one of the brokers used by Davila, denied any wrongdoing and said it was making the payment to end the dispute, in which Codelco alleged that brokers made secret commission payments to Davila.
"I would like to take this opportunity to restate the facts," said Becker in a statement faxed from Germany, where he lives.

He said he was neither dismissed by Merrill Lynch nor did he leave, as had been alleged, because of sweeping changes at the firm. "I had been asked to transfer to London to help manage the group's LME (London Metal Exchange) client business. I declined for personal reasons," he said.
He went on to say that, as both Sumitomo Corp of Japan and Codelco, were large users of the LME, it was not unusual for a broker to deal with both.
"Both Sumitomo and Codelco in turn dealt with a large number of brokers and not a 'handful' as alleged in some press reports," Becker wrote.

Becker said he was one of those involved in helping to evaluate the open and closed positions which Codelco had with a large number of brokers at the time it suspected it had lost money and "I believe that my help was invaluable in dealing with and curtailing those losses".
The joint statement by Merrill Lynch and Codelco stated that a vigorous and thorough investigation by the two firms found there was no evidence of improper payments, Becker said.
"I was not, of course, party to any negotiations nor was I investigated by Codelco," he added.
Becker recalled that a writ was issued by Codelco against him and others in April 1996 alleging the making of improper payments to Davila.
His statement added that these alleged improper payments were unrelated to the alleged unauthorized trading losses by the Chilean company that came to light in 1994.
"Proceedings are continuing in the Chancery Division of the High Court in London and continue to be vigorously defended," Becker said. - - Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
